paperInfo.subject: Agriculture
sourceBasis: ZIMSEC-style assessment formats and recurring syllabus areas
Original questions generated for this bank; not transcriptions of past papers
paperInfo.note: Original practice questions aligned to Agriculture syllabus coverage. They do not reproduce copyrighted past-paper text.

questions.questionText: A farmer plants 4 hectares at a seed rate of 12 kg/ha. What quantity of seed is required?
questions.explanation: Seed required = area × seed rate = 4 × 12 = 48 kg.

questions.questionText: A farmer obtains a soil pH of 6. Which amendment would generally be used to raise the pH of an acidic soil?
questions.explanation: Agricultural lime neutralises soil acidity and raises soil pH.

questions.questionText: Which operation should normally be carried out after sowing a crop when the main aim is to reduce competition from unwanted plants?
questions.explanation: Weeding removes or suppresses weeds so that the crop has less competition for light, water and nutrients.

questions.questionText: Which method is most appropriate for reducing the spread of a seed-borne fungal disease before planting?
questions.explanation: Certified treated seed reduces the risk of introducing seed-borne pathogens into the field.

questions.questionText: Which feature is most useful when selecting cattle for a beef-production enterprise?

options.text: Good growth rate and feed conversion

questions.explanation: Beef cattle are selected for desirable growth, carcass and feed-utilisation traits.

questions.questionText: Which nutrient is primarily required by livestock for body building, tissue repair and production of enzymes?
questions.explanation: Protein supplies amino acids needed for growth, tissue repair and many metabolic functions.

questions.questionText: Which observation would most strongly suggest that an animal requires veterinary attention?

options.text: Persistent loss of appetite and abnormal behaviour

questions.explanation: Persistent loss of appetite together with abnormal behaviour can indicate illness and warrants examination.

questions.questionText: Why are legumes valuable components of many pastures?

options.text: They can fix atmospheric nitrogen through symbiotic bacteria

questions.explanation: Legumes form symbiotic associations with nitrogen-fixing bacteria, improving nitrogen availability in the pasture.

questions.questionText: Which farm tool is primarily used for loosening soil and making planting holes on a small holding?
questions.explanation: A hoe is a common hand tool for loosening soil, making planting holes and controlling weeds.

questions.questionText: If total variable costs rise while output price and output remain unchanged, what happens to gross margin?
questions.explanation: Gross margin equals gross income minus variable costs, so higher variable costs reduce gross margin when other factors stay constant.

questions.questionText: A farmer plants 4 hectares at a seed rate of 13 kg/ha. What quantity of seed is required?
questions.explanation: Seed required = area × seed rate = 4 × 13 = 52 kg.

questions.questionText: Which record is most useful for determining the quantities of fertiliser purchased and used on a farm?
questions.explanation: An input record documents purchases and use of inputs such as fertiliser, seed and chemicals.

questions.questionText: Which practice is most effective for reducing soil erosion on sloping cultivated land?

options.text: Cultivating up and down the slope

questions.explanation: Contour cultivation slows runoff across slopes and helps reduce soil erosion.

questions.questionText: Which weather instrument is used to measure rainfall?
questions.explanation: A rain gauge measures the amount of precipitation received over a specified period.

questions.questionText: Which propagation method produces a new plant from a vegetative part of the parent plant rather than from a seed?
questions.explanation: A stem cutting is a vegetative propagation method in which a stem section develops roots and shoots.

questions.questionText: Which farm-management practice is most appropriate when a farmer wants to compare the performance of two enterprises using their costs and returns?
questions.explanation: Gross-margin analysis compares enterprise variable costs and returns and is used to support farm-management decisions.
